transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-13
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Riley Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Head of ML, Foxbridge), Leah Morgan (Platform Eng), Omar Aziz (CTO)

Summary: Quick renewal check and technical sync about moving part of traffic to Dedicated capacity and onboarding a private VPC for EU data flows.

[00:00] Riley Chen: Hey hey, thanks for carving out time. uh, we'll keep this tight, we know you all are heads down. Quick agenda — capacity bump request, VPC onboarding, and any compliance blockers.
[00:28] Daniel Park: Thanks Riley. Big things for us are predictable throughput during peak promotions and making sure the EU data never leaves our VPC. We've seen token spikes around the holiday test runs.
[01:02] Sofia Martinez: Got it. From the SE side we'll want to validate peak QPS and the 95th percentile tail. Do you have sample traffic or prompts we can run?
[01:25] Leah Morgan: Yeah we'll share a scrubbed prompt set — customer product descriptions, cart-totals and a few conversational flows. Also network topology and our firewall rules.
[01:46] Omar Aziz: I also want to highlight audit requirements — we need keystore integrations, KMS, and audit logs retained for 2 years. Is that part of the Private package?
[02:10] Riley Chen: Yep. For Private we support KMS integration and extended audit retention as an add-on. We'll put that in the proposal.
[02:36] Daniel Park: One thing — we heard from engineering that Dedicated was cheaper at scale but sometimes latency to EU is worse than the hosted multi-region offering. Can you walk through that?
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: Sure, it's a tradeoff. Hosted uses regional autoscaling and our multi-region edge routing so for small bursts it's lower latency if you hit the right region. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and consistent throughput, but if you colocate Dedicated in a single US region and serve EU traffic over WAN, you'll get higher RTT.
[03:33] (brief overlap) Daniel Park: Right, we want EU customers served inside the EU.
[03:48] Sofia Martinez: Exactly — for EU-only low latency you want Dedicated capacity in an EU geocluster or Private VPC deployed in your EU cloud project. That keeps token generation close and KV cache warm locally. Note: we sometimes see the transcriber label KV cash in older notes, um, that's KV cache.
[04:20] Riley Chen: To be pragmatic, our recommended path is: 1) short pilot with Private VPC in EU for critical routes, 2) synchronous Dedicated reservation for baseline traffic in EU region, 3) Hosted fallback for overflow to keep costs down.
[04:45] Leah Morgan: That makes sense. For the pilot — how long and what's the minimum reserved capacity?
[05:00] Sofia Martinez: Pilot typically 2–4 weeks. For reserved capacity we can show sizes — we usually recommend baseline of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for low-latency ecommerce tasks, but we will model your actual QPS.
[05:20] Daniel Park: 8 GPUs is, uh, significant. Cost sensitivity is high — our finance prefers a smaller commit if we can keep burst options.
[05:42] Riley Chen: We can structure a hybrid: smaller reserved commit + burstable pool pricing and a 6-month evaluation clause with an option to convert burst into reserved at a lower rate. I'll put numbers in the sheet.
[06:08] Omar Aziz: On security, SSO and RBAC integration are musts. We use Okta, SAML SSO. Is that supported for Private?
[06:26] Sofia Martinez: Yes, SAML/SSO via Okta is supported. For Private we also do customer-managed RBAC sync. We'll need an IdP metadata file.
[06:43] Leah Morgan: We'll send that. Also curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated is saturated, do requests go to hosted models or fail? We want graceful degradation.
[07:03] Sofia Martinez: By default we can configure automatic failover to a compatible hosted model variant. It can be configured per-route. So critical checkout flows would failover to a slightly cheaper or lower context model rather than returning errors.
[07:28] (small crosstalk) Daniel Park: That is good. We'd rather have slightly different quality than errors during peak.
[07:40] Riley Chen: And for audit — we can enable request-level logging and a dedicated audit stream to your SIEM, retention configurable.
[07:55] Omar Aziz: Perfect. On data residency, does Private VPC ensure model cache or logs aren't outside the VPC?
[08:10] Sofia Martinez: The runtime keeps KV cache in the local serving nodes. For Private, you control the nodes and network — logs and caches stay within your VPC unless you opt into cross-region replication. We will call out any managed control-plane metadata that may be stored in Redwood's control plane — we have a SOC 2 statement about minimal metadata.
[08:42] Leah Morgan: Could you send that SOC 2 statement and a diagram of what goes to Redwood control plane?
[08:55] Riley Chen: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC 2 summary and a control/data flow doc.
[09:10] Daniel Park: One practical ask — can you produce an estimated latency delta between a Hosted EU route vs Private VPC EU? We want numbers for our execs.
[09:29] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we'll run a bench with your prompts. Expect differences mostly in cold-start and KV cache priming. Warmed Dedicated in EU tends to be ~20–40ms faster p95 for the same token lengths compared to fall-through hosts, but we'll validate with your dataset.
[09:58] Riley Chen: Ok, so next up — timeline. You're looking to have this in place before Black Friday test windows, correct?
[10:12] Daniel Park: Ideally before Thanksgiving promo, so by end of November. Pilot in mid-November would be great.
[10:25] Riley Chen: Tight but doable. We'll aim for pilot week of 2027-11-22.
[10:34] (Speaker 3): Sounds good.
[11:00] Sofia Martinez: Quick technical note — firewall rules: we need allowlist for egress from your VPC to Redwood control plane IP ranges for provisioning. Leah, can you share the internal team who manages firewall changes?
[11:20] Leah Morgan: I'll add James from infra to the thread. He handles the network config.
[11:34] Riley Chen: Great. For the pricing ask — finance wanted a three-tier quote: small commit, medium commit, and enterprise commit with burst. We'll show cost per token for each and projected monthly run-rate.
[11:55] Daniel Park: And include the premium for extended log retention and KMS integration.
[12:05] Riley Chen: Yep. We'll enumerate add-on costs.
[12:20] Omar Aziz: Any competitors we should be comparing to? Our procurement mentioned LambdaStack and EdgeServe. How do you position vs them?
[12:33] Sofia Martinez: High level: LambdaStack has strong edge orchestration but fewer first-class model optimizations and higher complexity to operate. EdgeServe is competitive on price but typically lacks our observability and rollouts that matter for production. We'll attach a short comparison doc.
[12:55] Daniel Park: Good. One more technical item — can you support model pinning per route? We want canary and A/B testing.
[13:10] Sofia Martinez: Yes, rollouts and pinning are part of the Console. You can route certain traffic percentages to a canary model and automatically rollback on quality regressions.
[13:28] (overlap) Riley Chen: We'll propose a pilot that includes canary rollout for checkout flows.
[13:40] Leah Morgan: That helps. For legal, procurement asked about indemnity and data processing addenda. Who's the contact for the legal pack?
[13:53] Riley Chen: I'll have our commercial ops send the standard DPA, sublicense terms, and a tailored addendum for retention. Expect that in the proposal packet.
[14:10] Daniel Park: Ok. For the pilot acceptance criteria, what do you consider success?
[14:23] Sofia Martinez: Success criteria: sustained p95 latency below X ms for target routes, error rate below 0.1%, and cost per 1,000 tokens within the agreed bound. We'll define exact numbers once we run the baseline.
[14:44] Riley Chen: We'll propose measurable thresholds in the SOW.
[15:02] Omar Aziz: Any blockers you see from your side?
[15:09] Sofia Martinez: Nothing major; we just need the prompt set, allowlist, and an initial test key. We can stage a test environment with limited capacity.
[15:23] Daniel Park: We'll queue that up.
[16:00] Riley Chen: Quick note — we'll provide a sample run with 48-hour warm-up to prime KV cache; that often improves the p95 numbers.
[16:16] Daniel Park: Good call.
[16:30] Leah Morgan: Regarding billing, can we get invoices tied to cloud project IDs? We prefer chargeback to teams.
[16:45] Riley Chen: Yes, we can include billing metadata and per-team tags for chargeback reporting.
[17:00] (brief pause)
[17:20] Sofia Martinez: I'll start the benchmark once we get the test key and prompt set. Expect initial results within 48 hours.
[17:35] Daniel Park: Great.
[18:00] Riley Chen: Alright — to close, recap quick: Riley sends proposal and SOC2 + control flow doc; Sofia runs benchmark; Leah shares topology and allowlist; schedule pilot for week of 11/22. Any other urgent asks?
[18:26] Omar Aziz: None from me.
[18:30] Leah Morgan: We're good.
[18:45] Daniel Park: Thanks all.
[19:00] Riley Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread with dates.

End of transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional mislabels and minor word swaps (e.g., KV cash). Raw audio available in CRM if needed.
